translation_notes: 17 of the 18 term constructors are Literal(value, datatype=ShaclDataType.X.uri_ref): the datatype is a RUNTIME lookup through linkml's ShaclDataType enum, and ldpy has no interpolated-datatype form -- verified: f"{x}"^^xsd:time transpiles, but f"{x}"^^{dt} is rejected with "type de donnee attendu apres '^^'". This is the concrete language gap this example documents

expressing them would mean inlining the enum (f"{year}-{month}-{day}"^^xsd:date and so on), which is rejected as unfaithful: ShaclDataType is a shared domain abstraction and the inlining would erase the STRING / CURIE / NCNAME / JSON_POINTER / JSON_PATH / SPARQL_PATH distinctions, all six of which resolve to xsd:string
Literal(permissible_value_name) with no datatype also stays Python: bare {expr} coercion only exists inside g{} islands

the single op the notation does reach: URIRef(self.schema_view.expand_curie(default_value)) -> f<{self.schema_view.expand_curie(default_value)}> (exact, since no @base is in scope); `from rdflib import Literal, URIRef` loses URIRef. Arguably no clearer than the original -- same observation as the pyRdfa _URI example
no g{} island anywhere: the module is a term factory, it never asserts a triple

context shim: linkml is not installed; context.py holds ShaclDataType verbatim, a trimmed IfAbsentProcessor base (the class constants + constructor the region reaches), model stand-ins for the annotation-only names, and a DemoSchemaView. Import lines only, identical on both sides

demo harness added identically to both representations: it calls all 19 literal-producing paths (including both special-case branches of map_uri_or_curie/map_curie/map_uri) into a module-level demo_graph, and prints the tuple-returning and NotImplementedError paths so stdout is compared too
